web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the $16 Billion Engine — Specialty Pharmacy, LTC & Home Health
question: How does BrightSpring generate ~$12.9 billion in FY2025 (and ~$16.0 billion guided FY2026) revenue across Pharmacy Solutions and Provider Services, and what does a real-world patient episode look like in each segment?

epigraph.quote: Our third quarter results again reflect the commitment of our team to patient care and operational execution across our Pharmacy and Provider businesses... supported by a broad set of process and growth drivers across a uniquely scaled and high-quality platform.
epigraph.author: Jon Rousseau, CEO, BrightSpring Health Services (Q3 2026 Earnings Release)

web_blocks.title: 2.1 Segment Architecture & Revenue/EBITDA Mix (Post-Community Living Divestiture)

web_blocks.html: Following the March 30, 2026 sale of ResCare Community Living, BrightSpring reports two continuing segments: Pharmacy Solutions and Provider Services [1, 26]. Community Living is now classified as discontinued operations [1, 26]. In FY2025, consolidated continuing revenue reached $12,910.6 million, up 28.2% year-over-year [1, 3]. Adjusted EBITDA totaled $617.6 million, up 34.2% year-over-year [1, 3]. By Q3 2026, annualized revenue had passed $16.8 billion [27]. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $15.9–$16.125 billion and Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $850–$860 million [27].

Pharmacy Solutions is the main top-line and profit engine. It generated 88.7% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, or ~$11.45 billion (+30.7% YoY) [1, 3], and $10,311.0 million (+24.4% YoY) in 9M 2026 (88.1% of $11,700.1 million consolidated 9M revenue, per the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q) [26]. The segment has two sub-lines. First, Infusion and Specialty Pharmacy makes up 74.3% of 9M 2026 consolidated revenue ($3,179.8 million in Q3 2026, +33.8% YoY), led by Onco360 in oncology and CareMed in rare and chronic disease [9, 26, 27]. Second, Home and Community Pharmacy accounts for 13.8% of 9M 2026 revenue ($552.6 million in Q3 2026, -6.3% YoY) [26]. Anchored by PharMerica, this sub-line absorbed a $138.0 million (-7.9% YoY) nine-month revenue drop (-$37.4 million in Q3 alone) driven by Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) Medicare Part D price negotiations, rebates, and statutory caps alongside higher fulfillment cost per script [26, 33].

Provider Services contributes 11.3% of FY2025 consolidated revenue, or ~$1.46 billion (+11.1% YoY) [1, 3], and scaled to $1,389.1 million (+29.7% YoY) in 9M 2026 ($480.8 million in Q3 2026, +31.0% YoY) [26, 27]. Core lines include Home Health Care & Hospice, where average daily census reached 47,256 in Q3 2026 (+57.6% YoY vs. 29,980) after integrating 107 Amedisys and LHC branches [8, 27]. The segment also runs Rehabilitation Care (7,574 persons served in Q3 2026, +9.3% YoY) and Personal Care (16,320 persons served, +1.2% YoY) [27]. Yet rapid expansion has carried integration friction: in 9M 2026, Provider Services SG&A rose 38.0% YoY ($379.5 million vs. $275.0 million), outpacing +29.7% revenue growth and holding Provider Segment EBITDA margin nearly flat at 15.8% (vs. 15.7% in 9M 2025) [26].

web_blocks.title: 2.2 Concrete End-to-End Examples Across Every Operating Line

web_blocks.html: Example 1 — Pharmacy Solutions (Specialty Oncology via Onco360): Picture a patient newly diagnosed with Stage IV lung cancer or neurofibromatosis type 1. The doctor prescribes a new targeted oral kinase inhibitor that carries strict Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) rules [9]. The drug is restricted to a Limited Distribution Drug (LDD) panel of just 3 to 5 national pharmacies [9]. When the oncologist sends the e-prescription to Onco360, the Louisville hub begins 'Total Protocol Management' [9]. Staff verify medical and pharmacy benefits, file prior authorizations, and enroll the patient in copay or foundation grants [9]. A board-certified oncology pharmacist checks for drug interactions and ships temperature-controlled pills overnight [9]. Those high-dollar scripts lifted consolidated pharmacy revenue per script to $263.93 in FY2025 [3]. They also support manufacturer data fees and dispensing gross profit of $28.86 per script by Q3 2026 [3, 9, 27].

Example 2 — Pharmacy Solutions (Home & Community LTC via PharMerica): Consider an 82-year-old skilled nursing facility (SNF) resident recovering from hip surgery with diabetes and heart failure. Instead of managing twelve retail bottles, PharMerica's regional closed-door pharmacy links straight to the facility's electronic health record [3, 9]. Staff pack daily doses into barcode-verified multi-dose blister packs or unit-dose strips, while consultant pharmacists review regimens monthly and couriers deliver 24/7 stat kits [3, 9]. Unit economics are far tighter here than in oncology: IRA Part D negotiated prices and statutory caps cut Home and Community revenue by $138.0 million (-7.9% YoY) across 9M 2026, while fulfillment cost per script rose [26, 33]. Even so, PharMerica's dense closed-door route network keeps core facility contracts sticky [4, 9].

Example 3 — Provider Services (Home Health & Infusion / Rehab): Imagine a 74-year-old Medicare patient discharged home after septic knee surgery. The patient needs six weeks of intravenous antibiotics and physical therapy. BrightSpring's Adoration Home Health branch coordinates the hospital discharge, potentially from one of the 107 acquired Amedisys/LHC sites [8, 27]. A skilled nurse visits the home for IV care and wound checks [8, 27]. In-home physical therapists help restore mobility, while BrightSpring's infusion pharmacy compounds and ships the IV drug [8, 27]. Keeping the patient out of a $2,500-a-day hospital bed or $500-a-day SNF bed saves payers money [8, 27]. That alignment drives steady referrals from Medicare and managed-care plans [8, 27].

web_blocks.title: 2.3 Revenue Mix vs. Profit Mix & Cross-Segment Referral Synergy

web_blocks.html: Judging BrightSpring by revenue mix alone hides both where cash profits originate and where hidden cost friction sits [1, 3, 26]. Because Onco360 dispenses high-cost oncology drugs (lifting consolidated revenue per script 24.0% YoY to $340.86 in Q3 2026), Pharmacy Solutions makes up 88.1% of 9M 2026 revenue at an 8.5% Q3 segment gross margin and 5.3% 9M Segment EBITDA margin ($551.1 million) [26, 27]. Provider Services carries minimal drug pass-through cost and generated $219.8 million of 9M 2026 Segment EBITDA (15.8% margin, or 28.5% of total Segment EBITDA on 11.9% of sales) [26, 27]. At the same time, unallocated corporate overhead remains a material drag: 9M 2026 unallocated corporate SG&A ex-D&A reached $239.7 million ($148 million Adjusted Corporate Costs, up 28% YoY from $116 million), while company-wide Adjusted EBITDA excluded $15.6 million of acquisition/integration costs and $25.8 million of restructuring/divestiture expenses across the first nine months of 2026 [26, 27].

Operationally, both segments reinforce each other at hospital discharge and during chronic care [8, 27]. Complex patients leaving acute hospitals often need both compounded home infusions and skilled nursing visits [8, 27]. BrightSpring's home health and hospice network now spans ~30 states [8, 27]. It served 31,135 average daily patients in FY2025 and grew ADC 58% year-over-year in Q3 2026 [3, 27]. That reach lets BrightSpring capture both medication and clinical-care referrals as a single post-acute partner [3, 8, 27]. Meanwhile, Rehab Without Walls (~7,127 persons served) and Personal Care (~16,079 persons served) extend care into neuro-rehab and daily support [3]. Those services deepen ties with local hospitals and Medicare Advantage plans [3, 8, 27].

book_paragraphs: If you only glance at BrightSpring's revenue split, it looks like a pure drug distributor. Pharmacy Solutions supplies 88.7% of its $12.9 billion in FY2025 continuing sales ($11,452 million). Provider Services supplies only 11.3% ($1,459 million). That top-line ratio is misleading because specialty drug prices are huge while service labor is smaller per episode. Look one layer deeper at gross profit and segment EBITDA. In Q4 2025, Pharmacy Solutions generated $162 million in segment EBITDA, while Provider Services generated $64 million. Provider Services punches nearly three times above its revenue weight, contributing ~28% of segment EBITDA on just over a tenth of sales.

Let's walk through how those businesses work on the ground, starting with Onco360 and CareMed. Together, they anchor Pharmacy Solutions' $9.1 billion Infusion and Specialty sub-line, or 70.5% of consolidated sales. Picture a patient in Ohio newly diagnosed with Stage IV lung cancer or a rare genetic disorder. The doctor prescribes a new oral kinase inhibitor that costs $15,000 a month and carries strict FDA REMS rules. The drugmaker does not send that pill to a corner retail chain. Instead, it limits distribution to a Limited Distribution Drug (LDD) panel of three to five elite specialty pharmacies.

When the oncologist sends that e-prescription to Onco360's Louisville hub, the real work starts before a pill ships. A dedicated team runs 'Total Protocol Management.' Staff verify whether the drug falls under the medical or pharmacy benefit and file prior authorizations. They also secure manufacturer copay cards or charity grants so the patient won't abandon care over a $2,000 out-of-pocket bill. Next, an oncology pharmacist checks drug interactions, counsels the patient 24/7 on side effects, and ships temperature-controlled doses overnight. That clinical service lifted pharmacy revenue per script 26.1% to $263.93 in FY2025. It also raised pharmacy gross profit per script 21.4% to $21.64 in FY2025 and 27% to $28.86 in Q3 2026.

Now contrast that oncology hub with PharMerica, the Home and Community Pharmacy unit at 13.8% of 9M 2026 revenue. Picture an 82-year-old nursing-home resident recovering from hip surgery with diabetes and heart failure. Instead of juggling twelve retail bottles, PharMerica's closed-door pharmacy plugs directly into the facility's electronic health record. Staff pack daily doses into barcode-verified blister packs or automated unit-dose strips, consultant pharmacists review regimens monthly, and couriers deliver 24/7 stat emergency kits. It is sticky infrastructure, yet government pricing pressure bites hardest here. Rather than a one-quarter Q1 blip, Medicare Part D changes under the Inflation Reduction Act cut Home and Community revenue by $138.0 million (-7.9% year-over-year) across the first nine months of 2026, including a $37.4 million (-6.3%) decline in Q3 alone, alongside higher fulfillment cost per script.

Finally, step inside Provider Services—home health, hospice, neuro-rehab (~7,127 patients), and personal care (~16,079 patients). In late 2025, BrightSpring paid $239 million for 107 Amedisys and LHC Group branches. That deal nearly doubled its home health footprint from 14 states to roughly 30. It also drove Q3 2026 average daily census up 58% year-over-year from a FY2025 base of ~31,135 patients. Picture a 74-year-old Medicare patient sent home after septic knee surgery who needs six weeks of IV antibiotics and physical therapy. Instead of staying in a $2,500-a-day hospital bed or $500-a-day nursing home, a BrightSpring Adoration nurse visits the home. The nurse handles wound care and IV lines while BrightSpring's infusion pharmacy compounds and delivers the antibiotics.

Why does this two-segment model work better together than apart—and where does unit-economic friction creep in? Complex post-acute patients rarely need just a pill or just a nurse. Pharmacy Solutions scaled to $10,311.0 million in 9M 2026 revenue (+24.4% YoY) and $551.1 million of Segment EBITDA (5.3% margin), with Q3 revenue per script jumping 24% to $340.86 on 33.8% Specialty and Infusion growth. Meanwhile, Provider Services grew 9M 2026 revenue 29.7% to $1,389.1 million and generated $219.8 million of Segment EBITDA (15.8% margin, 28.5% of total segment EBITDA). Yet two hidden frictions bear watching. First, Provider Services SG&A jumped 38.0% year-over-year in 9M 2026 ($379.5 million vs. $275.0 million) due to Amedisys/LHC branch integration, wage costs, and transition service fees, keeping Provider EBITDA margin flat at 15.8% despite the 57.6% ADC surge. Second, unallocated corporate costs rose to $148 million in 9M 2026 (up 28% YoY), while Adjusted EBITDA excluded $41.3 million of 9M integration, transaction, and restructuring charges.

Let's also trace a real-world Rehab Without Walls and Personal Care episode so those smaller units don't get overlooked. Picture a forty-five-year-old patient recovering from a traumatic brain injury or stroke after hospital discharge. Instead of staying in a sub-acute rehab facility far from family, Rehab Without Walls sends occupational, physical, and speech therapists into the home. Therapists train the patient to climb stairs, manage daily routines, and regain independence. Meanwhile, Personal Care aides help roughly 16,079 people nationwide with bathing, meals, and medication reminders. Those services lack the headline size of a $15,000 oncology script, yet they deepen ties with state Medicaid plans and Medicare Advantage coordinators.

Keep that contrast in mind whenever you read a BrightSpring earnings release. If you only check consolidated gross margin (~11.8% in FY2025), you will misread the business. Every new $15,000 oncology script at Onco360 inflates revenue and pulls percentage gross margin down, even while adding $28.86+ of gross profit dollars. Watch the two-engine dashboard instead. Track Infusion and Specialty revenue growth (+34% YoY in Q3 2026) alongside Provider Services census growth (+58% YoY in Q3 2026) and Adjusted EBITDA scaling toward $850–$860 million in FY2026.

book_callouts.title: Revenue Mix vs. Profit Mix
book_callouts.text: High-ticket specialty drugs inflate top-line revenue ($263.93 per script in FY2025) and compress optical gross margins (~11.8%). Never judge a specialty pharmacy by its percentage gross margin alone—watch gross profit dollars per script ($21.64 in FY25 -> $28.86 in Q3 26) alongside Provider Services' higher-margin clinical EBITDA.
